queries.sql:
SELECT toString(`id`) AS `id`, toString(`customer`) AS `customer`, toString(`amount`) AS `amount`, toString(`status`) AS `status`, toString(`metadata`) AS `metadata`, toString(toTimeZone(`updated_at`, 'UTC')) AS `updated_at`, toString(`_peerdb_version`) AS __rg_version,
                    toString(`_peerdb_is_deleted`) AS __rg_deleted FROM (
                    SELECT *, dense_rank() OVER (PARTITION BY `id` ORDER BY `_peerdb_version` DESC) AS __rg_rank
                    FROM `orders`) WHERE __rg_rank = 1

verification.fault: Destination rows deliberately altered by this lab. No upstream PeerDB bug is claimed.

benchmarks.method: Synthetic three-column journal, 10% one-row updates, exact matching target. Three warm-cache runs including process startup; macOS time -l peak RSS bytes. Inspect does not keep history. Audit retains state and reconstructs histories only for discrepant keys. Python baseline checks CRC/SHA and exact scalar equality but supports only this fixture schema; it is not a full feature competitor.

benchmark_summary.title: 100,000 rows in 0.44 seconds
benchmark_summary.description: Native audit: 0.44 s median, 198 MiB peak memory. The restricted Python reference was faster at 0.30 s, using 256 MiB. Three warm-cache runs on macOS arm64; synthetic three-column rows and 10% updates. These measure reconstruction and comparison, not WAL transport or fsync throughput.
